families.reason: OE Hebrew/Aramaic chapter files: morphhb lemma and morphology CC BY 4.0, WLC text public domain, hebrew-bible text GPL-3.0. Attribution travels in the oe edition record.
Per-book raw OE files are the source of the included chapter files; normalizing both would duplicate every passage.

Delitzsch 1885 Hebrew New Testament as carried by the DHNT'85+ module in data/delitzsch/raw, the source the parser reads. The module's info table states 'Copyright Public Domain. Delitzsch, Franz, 1885'; that self-declaration is the only license evidence in the repository, and docs/terms.md has no row for the Delitzsch text. Passage text is the parsed verse with prefix-segmentation slashes removed, which reproduces the module text for all 7,956 verses. Word surfaces are kept; Strong's codes and prefixes are withheld (see delitzsch-strongs).
The per-word Strong's mapping in the parsed Delitzsch files originates from ph4.org, whose license is unclear (site copyright 2005-2026 Ph4).
The DHNT'85+ SQLite module is the source of the included parsed chapters. Its text is normalized through them; its embedded Strong's tags fall under delitzsch-strongs.

Per-book files of a different Delitzsch edition (metadata publication_year 1877) read only by the legacy parser path. With segmentation removed and both texts NFC-normalized, 6,209 of 7,956 verses differ from the parsed 1885 text. Contract v1 has one Delitzsch edition, so this edition is deferred.
Review decisions are lexical adjudication and dictionary work, which this normalization excludes.
Committed SBLGNT reading with STEPBible TAGNT tags, both CC BY 4.0 with required notices that travel in the sblgnt-tagnt edition record.
TBESG / UBS lexicon of the committed Greek release. Only entry identifiers and lemmas are normalized; definitions are never copied.
Runtime bundle copies, lexicon shards, occurrence indexes and release metadata derived from the same Greek release; the release chapters and lexicon are normalized directly.
Official STEPBible/UBS downloads and importer outputs are ignored by Git and are not inputs.
Open Scriptures Hebrew Lexicon CC BY 4.0 with public-domain BDB/Strong's. Only entry identifiers and lemmas are normalized; definitions are never copied.
Torah con Yehoshua' Hamashiaj definitions were given to the project owner as permission to use, not to redistribute.
Raw lexicon sources, per-book word lists, prefixes, roots, translations and reports are dictionary population and adjudication inputs, which this normalization excludes.
SPABES Spanish Bible, CC BY 4.0 with attribution in the bes-es edition record. Native verse labels are kept; no mapping is inferred.
The USFX file is the source of the included per-book JSON; normalizing both would duplicate passages.
Licensed TTH translation, restricted pending the Doldan agreement. The existing pilot inputs stay unchanged; no new normalized TTH artifacts are produced.
Licensed ISR text, served from Supabase Storage and ignored by Git; not present in the repository.
Qumran data has no stated license and docs/terms.md treats it as non-redistributable; a .gitignore comment claims CC BY-SA 4.0. The conflict is unresolved.
The contract lists the Hutter connector as not implemented, and the committed data is a staging transcription pipeline rather than a reviewed edition.
Transliteration is a second annotation layer over OE and Delitzsch tokens; contract v1 has no record kind for it. DSS transliterations also inherit the dss restriction.
The contextual relationship catalog is owned by #184.
The Shaul commentary search corpus is generated and ignored by Git; its public source notes are normalized directly as shaul-notes.
Public Shaul knowledge records at the pinned revision.
Public Shaul notes under content/besorah, content/tanaj and content/temas at the pinned revision.
Shaul navigation pages, the content placeholder and authoring templates are not notes.
Shaul generated/ graphs and data/ authoring inventories are derived metadata, not source records.
Private transcripts and local-only Shaul records are excluded entirely.
Shaul docs/scriptures mirrors Davar OE, Delitzsch and TTH files for local verse sheets. It carries TTH, which is restricted; the OE and Delitzsch copies are normalized from Davar directly.
